title: Federated trace proxy + sharded metrics gateway for Dedicated/VPC observability
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight federated trace proxy and sharded metrics gateway that can be deployed inside customer VPCs / on-prem clusters for Dedicated and Private customers. The proxy/gateway will provide tenant-scoped routing, enforce mTLS and API key auth to Redwood control plane (optional), support configurable sampling rules and adaptive buffering for backpressure, and expose a local, low-cost aggregation layer for latency/error dashboards without sending raw full-fidelity telemetry off-cluster by default.

Why: Current solutions rely on a single forwarder or generic agents that either ship all telemetry off-cluster (cost/security concerns) or provide poor tenant isolation. This work reduces cross-tenant blast radius, lowers egress and storage costs for private deployments, and preserves high-fidelity traces for SLO debug paths with explicit, auditable offload rules.

Scope:
- A small Go-based trace proxy that accepts OTLP/http and gRPC traces, applies tenant binding (from request headers, sidecar identity, or local config), and forwards sampled spans to central ingestion or to a local aggregation store.
- A sharded metrics gateway that performs per-tenant metric aggregation, rate limiting, and delta compression before forwarding to Redwood’s metrics pipeline.
- Configurable sampling and retention policies per-customer and per-route; ability to escalate traces to full-fidelity for incidents.
- Local persistence buffer with backpressure-aware admission control and configurable disk limits.
- Admin endpoints for health, metrics, and an audit stream of offload decisions.

Non-goals: building a full-featured collector with every exporter. We will support a small matrix of exporters (OTLP, Prometheus remote_write) and provide hooks for customers to plug additional exporters in later.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OTLP traces and preserves tenant_id for every span when tenant binding is available
Gateway aggregates counter/gauge deltas and reduces egress by >= 60% on typical private deployment workload
Config-driven sampling rules applied with <50ms median additional latency
Local buffering survives a 30-minute network outage and replays without duplication
Audit log contains per-span and per-metric offload decision for SRE review
implementation_notes: Prototype runtime in Go using otelcol components for ingestion, custom routing layer for tenant binding
Persist buffers to local RocksDB for small footprint and fast replay; consider leveldb if RocksDB licensing or size is a blocker
Use consistent-hash sharding for metrics gateway to enable horizontal scaling across nodes in private clusters
Expose mTLS and token auth; integrate with customer KMS for key rotation where provided
Keep binary <50MB for air-gapped install and provide helm chart and bare-manifest options
tradeoffs_and_risks: Local buffering increases disk usage—need conservative defaults and clear doc for customers
Sampling at the edge loses some global context for tail-sampling; mitigate with an escalation workflow to request full traces for incidents
Implementing many exporters increases maintenance; initial launch will target OTLP and prometheus remote_write
Sharding introduces complexity for cross-tenant queries across nodes; provide a lightweight coordinator for central queries
progress_updates: 2025-02-07: Spike complete. Validated OTLP ingress and a minimal forward+buffer loop in k8s using otelcol components (Ava)
2025-02-10: Design review with Security and Infra. Security requested explicit audit events for offload decisions and configurable default to never offload for high-compliance customers (Sanjay)
2025-02-14: Implemented prototype metrics delta compression. Initial egress reduction ~68% on internal workload (benchmark run #3) (Ben F.)
2025-02-18: Integration test for 30min network partition + replay successful in CI environment; observed duplicate suppression via idempotent replay tokens (QA)
2025-02-20: Merged initial helm chart and created internal alpha release artifacts. Preparing rollout plan for 2 pilot customers (Ava)
review_feedback: Security (Maya): require security_review_required=true and add a threat model section to the design doc
SRE (Liam): add per-tenant circuit breaker with exponential backoff to avoid noisy neighbor issues
Product (Evelyn): expose a toggle in Console to control per-customer offload policy and a cost estimation for choosing local vs central retention
